title: N-able takes cloud platform offline after 30+ "zero-days" published
content_md: N-able has taken its hosted N-central environments offline and urged on-premises customers to shut down their servers after a security researcher publicly disclosed more than 30 alleged zero-day vulnerabilities, including exploits that could let attackers take over vulnerable systems. Security researcher Sean Bales disclosed the vulnerabilities late Sunday, November 8, and published a GitHub repository called Able2Shell containing proof-of-concept exploits for the flaws. N-central is a remote monitoring and management (RMM) platform used by managed service providers (MSPs) and IT teams to monitor, manage, and secure customer devices and networks remotely. The researcher says the vulnerabilities were tested against N-central Appliance 2026.4.0.31, a pre-release version of the software, and believes most, if not all, flaws also affect earlier versions. Bales also confirmed to BleepingComputer that the discovery of the vulnerabilities was AI-assisted. The disclosed vulnerabilities include authentication bypasses, credential disclosure, arbitrary file writes, directory traversal, cross-site scripting (XSS), XML external entity (XXE) injection, and remote code execution (RCE) flaws. One of the most critical exploit chains abuses an unauthenticated XXE vulnerability in N-central's service-import functionality to steal a trusted local session, reset an account password, and execute commands on the server as the nable user.
